d.x: He was so angry that he hucked the book at my face.

d.d: To throw oneself off a large jump or drop.
To throw one's body in the air, possibly in a way that is ungraceful or lacks skill.
A long throw, generally at least half a field in length.
A drop or jump off a cliff or cornice.
A small round fruit of a dark blue or red color, of several plants in the related genera Vaccinium and Gaylussacia.
A small amount, a short distance, as in the phrase huckleberry above a persimmon.
A peddler or hawker, who sells small items, either door-to-door, from a stall, or in the street.
Somebody who sells things in an aggressive or showy manner.
One who deceptively sells fraudulent products; snake oil salesman.
To haggle, to wrangle, or to bargain.
To sell or offer (goods) from place to place, to peddle.
To promote or sell (goods) in an aggressive, showy manner.
third-person singular simple present indicative of huckster
